transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Emma Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Quantaco Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Quantaco Infra), Priya Shah (Quantaco PM)

Summary: Weekly POC cost/unit-economics review. Reviewed tokens/sec/$ baselines, caching results from last week's run, discussed batching tradeoffs and latency SLOs, agreed on next benchmarking sweep and action items.

Topics: cost per 1k tokens, prefix/K V cache savings, batching vs p90 latency, dedicated vs hosted cost delta, quantization and perf tradeoffs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma Chen: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — recap last week's benchmarks, dig into cost per token numbers, look at the caching results, then decide the next test sweep. sound good?
[00:18] Lina Park: yep sounds good. we want to make sure the numbers reflect our traffic shape — a lot of short prompts but occasional long contexts for convo histories.
[00:27] Carlos Ruiz: got it. i'll call out what we ran last week: baseline (no cache, batch=4), model v1-quant-16 and v1-8 quantized variants. we measured tokens/sec and token-cost based on the reserved GPU pricing in the spreadsheet.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: quick q — is the spreadsheet using dedicated reserved pricing or hosted on-demand? that changes the per-token $ significantly.
[00:52] Emma Chen: good call — current sheet shows a blended view: hosted list price for small workloads and an estimated reserved commit discount for Dedicated. i'll send a clearer split after this call.
[01:05] Priya Shah: also, for product planning we need p90 latency at under 450ms for short prompts, can you show how batching impacts that?
[01:15] Carlos Ruiz: yeah, so tradeoff in short — larger batch sizes push tokens/sec up, so tokens per dollar improves, but p90 climbs. last week batch 8 gave ~32% better tokens/sec/$ vs batch 1, but p90 jumped from ~220ms to ~620ms in our baseline test.
[01:40] Lina Park: ouch 620ms is too high for our interactive flow. we could accept that for async workloads but not for the chat widget.
[01:48] Emma Chen: agreed. that's where prefix cache helps — remember the prefix cache numbers? with prefix/K V caching on, the backend avoided re-computing the history for 60% of requests in our simulated trace and that dropped effective tokens per inference by about 28%.
[02:05] Marcus Lee: when you say K V cache, transcripts sometimes show 'K V' or 'KV' — just to be clear that's key-value attention cache on the model side, not an external cache tier, correct?
[02:20] Carlos Ruiz: correct — it's the model kv cache. though we also simulate a separate prefix cache on the request router that avoids sending prefix tokens at all. both layers add up.
[02:32] Priya Shah: our product metric is cost per 1k tokens normalized to user-perceived responses. can we get a table where you show raw tokens generated vs billed tokens after cache savings?
[02:43] Emma Chen: yes — i'll update the sheet to include 'billed tokens' column (post-cache) and tokens/sec/$ normalization. link I'll share: drive.redwood/quantaco/costs (I'll email it after).
[02:55] Lina Park: also curious about quantization impact — we saw model v1-8 had slightly worse quality on our eval set but cheaper. what's the perf delta?
[03:05] Carlos Ruiz: v1-8 (8-bit) did reduce memory and improved throughput in some kernels — tokens/sec improved ~12% vs 16-bit quantized run, but we saw small regen quality diffs on the hallucination set — think about safety threshold.
[03:20] Marcus Lee: are those kernels stable on our infra? we run on mixed GPU types, A100 and H100 in our cloud account. some kernels are optimized for H100.
[03:30] Carlos Ruiz: kernel selection is automatic in the runtime — but real-world perf differs by hardware. in our tests we used a single H100-equivalent cluster. we should run a mixed-hardware sweep to mirror your fleet.
[03:45] Emma Chen: ok next test: Carlos will run batch sweep with cache on/off across kernels and hardware profile that Marcus will provide.
[03:54] Marcus Lee: i'll export a 7-day sample of production traces — seq length distribution, percentiles, traffic bursts. expect that by Friday.
[04:03] Priya Shah: what about the fallback policy? if cache misses or busy queue causes latency spike, can Redwood route to a cheaper/faster variant?
[04:12] Carlos Ruiz: yes, we support smart routing — policy can route by latency tier or cost tier to downgraded model variant. we can demo automatic fallback in the deep dive.
[04:20] Lina Park: from a cost perspective, what was the net tokens/sec/$ we measured with prefix cache enabled?
[04:26] Carlos Ruiz: rough number from last run: baseline tokens/sec/$ = 1.0 (normalized). with prefix cache it went to ~1.32 — so ~32% improvement. with batching bumping to 8 and cache on, it was closer to 1.6 but again latency cost.
[04:41] Emma Chen: to translate to $ — at your projected 50M monthly tokens, that delta matters. we'll add scenario rows in the sheet (hosted vs dedicated reserved x1.2 commit vs x0.8) so you can see monthly bill swings.
[04:57] Marcus Lee: dedicated committed pricing looks attractive if we hit steady throughput, but commit risk is our concern. what's the minimum commit Redwood recommends?
[05:07] Emma Chen: depends on your peaks, but we usually see customers commit to 30-40% of expected sustained load to get meaningful discounts while retaining burst capacity. Carlos can quantify with your trace.
[05:20] Carlos Ruiz: yes i'll run the simulation — put your 7-day trace into our cost model and we'll show commit tiers effects.
[05:27] Priya Shah: can we also get the end-to-end p99 numbers with batching? p90 we discussed, but p99 heavy tails matter for SLOs.
[05:36] Carlos Ruiz: absolutely — batching increases tail latency more than median. i'll capture p50/p90/p99 for each sweep and include in the CSV.
[05:44] Lina Park: any security or audit implications of caching? we have strict data retention needs.
[05:50] Emma Chen: good question — cache items are ephemeral in the runtime and not stored in long-term storage. for Private deployments we can configure KMS and retention policies; for hosted we redact sensitive fields per the security doc. i'll attach the doc after the call (link: redwood.com/security/quantaco).
[06:05] Marcus Lee: sounds good. also curious about the performance of prefix cache when convo history grows — our threads can be 3k tokens frequently. how does cache hit rate behave?
[06:15] Carlos Ruiz: hit rate drops as history diverges. we saw in synthetic tests that if histories are highly unique hit rate falls to ~20-30%, but even then you save on repeated system prompts or templates. we should run with your real traces.
[06:31] Emma Chen: circling back to batching tradeoffs — one idea: hybrid routing. route low-latency short prompts to batch=1 fast path, and longer/async workloads to larger batch pools. that keeps frontend latency low while saving cost on the heavy tails.
[06:50] Priya Shah: that's appealing. does Redwood support per-route configs?
[06:54] Carlos Ruiz: yes per-route SLOs, per-route batching and cache policy. we can provide a config template.
[07:02] Lina Park: ok practical question — what's the expected time to run the test suite you propose? how long before we get updated numbers?
[07:10] Carlos Ruiz: if Marcus sends the trace by Friday we can run the mixed-hardware and batch sweep in ~48 hours and share a results CSV. so by next Tuesday morning you should have it.
[07:20] Emma Chen: timeline noted — send sheet and i'll incorporate scenario rows; Carlos will post the bench CSV and raw logs; Marcus will send traces; we'll reconvene next week.
[07:28] Marcus Lee: another small note — our infra team is sensitive to cold-start on warm pools; did you simulate cold-start penalties?
[07:35] Carlos Ruiz: our default tests use warm pools. cold-start penalties vary by model and infra state; we can run a small experiment with scaling down to 0 and measuring warmup time if you want.
[07:46] Priya Shah: yes please — add that as optional test.
[07:50] Emma Chen: added as action item.
[07:55] Lina Park: any blockers from Redwood side on running the cache-on tests?
[08:01] Carlos Ruiz: no blockers — we just need the production-like trace and confirmation of hardware mix. also permission to use quantaco eval set for quality checks on quantized variants.
[08:12] Lina Park: granted — share how we'll handle data access and retention.
[08:16] Emma Chen: i'll include the security/PII handling note in the doc email.
[08:21] Carlos Ruiz: quick note on measurement: we'll report tokens/sec/$ as tokens per second divided by effective $/sec based on the pricing model row. that gives normalized tokens per dollar; then we'll show cost per 1k billed tokens for your usage scenarios.
[08:36] Marcus Lee: sounds good — also, can you include an assumption row for cache hit distribution? i.e. optimistic 60%, realistic 35%, conservative 15%.
[08:45] Emma Chen: yes we'll include three scenarios.
[08:49] Priya Shah: lastly, what about fallbacks to cheaper models — is there a drop in quality metrics we can quantify?
[08:56] Carlos Ruiz: we'll add regen-quality diffs on a small eval set (ROUGE/QA accuracy + hand-sampled examples) across quantization and cheaper variants.
[09:07] Emma Chen: ok wrapping — recap of action items and owners, and we'll sync next Tuesday same time for results.
[09:14] Lina Park: thanks everyone.
[09:16] Marcus Lee: thanks.
[09:17] Priya Shah: thanks, bye.
[09:20] Emma Chen: bye all, I'll follow up with the sheet and links.

End of transcript.
